title: Tenant cost fairness + cache-warmth dashboard — quicknotes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note for designing a compact dashboard and metric set that answers the core question: are we charging / reporting cost to tenants in a way that reflects true GPU work and cache effectiveness? Also capture quick tracing anchors to diagnose perceived unfairness ("why did tenant A pay more than tenant B for similar throughput").

TL;DR / mission:
- Produce a minimal set of metrics and dashboard widgets that show per-tenant amortized GPU cost, per-call cache-warmth, and an adjusted requests-per-token rate that factors batching and shared KV cache hits.
- Add trace anchors for cold-cache flows and tenant-fanout to correlate cost spikes with traceable events.
- Keep the dashboard small (6–8 widgets) for quick triage by platform and SRE oncall.

Audience:
- Platform/SRE oncall (fast triage)
- Billing team (high-level attribution)
- Solutions/Account teams (investigate customer questions)
- Engineers running experiments that change batching/quantization/cache config

Design constraints and assumptions (working):
- We only have access to per-request metadata: tenant_id, model_name, model_version, sequence_length, token_count_generated, timestamps for receive/dispatch/completion, kv_cache_hit boolean, batch_id, batch_size, and GPU kernel milliseconds (per-request aggregation from runtime).
- No perfect per-request GPU-cycle accounting — we approximate by attributing batch-level GPU time across requests weighted by token_count and an estimate of kv cache savings.
- Sample rate for detailed traces should be small to keep trace volume manageable; we will bias-sample cold-cache requests and requests that exceed 95th percentile latency.

Core metric definitions (canonical names and short intent):
- tenant_gpu_ms_total: cumulative GPU milliseconds attributed to tenant (approx). Aggregation: sum over batch_gpu_ms * (tenant_token_count_in_batch / total_tokens_in_batch). Intent: primary cost denominator.
- tenant_tokens_total: number of generated tokens attributed to tenant. Aggregation: sum(token_count_generated). Intent: unit for cost-per-token.
- tenant_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd_est: (tenant_gpu_ms_total * gpu_rate_per_ms) / (tenant_tokens_total / 1000). Intent: relative cost metric for billing/QA.
- tenant_kv_cache_hit_rate: ratio of requests for tenant with kv_cache_hit=true. Window: 5m rolling. Intent: higher hit rate -> lower marginal cost.
- per_request_cache_warmth_index: score 0..1 where 0=cold (no prefix/KV reuse), 1=hot (full KV hit). Implementation: (kv_cache_hit ? 1 : recent_prompt_hash_seen_in_window(prompt_hash, tenant) ? 0.5 : 0). Intent: quick signal to explain latency/cost deltas at request level.
- shard_batch_efficiency: avg(batch_size * avg_seq_length) per shard per minute. Intent: detect uneven batching dilution across tenants.
- tenant_amortized_host_overhead_ms: platform overhead (network, pre/post-processing) amortized per-tenant. Intent: separate infra overhead from pure GPU time.

Dashboard widget proposals (compact 6 widgets):
1) Top-level cost heatmap (matrix): tenants on Y, models on X. Cell = tenant_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd_est (last 1h). Quick view to spot outliers. 
2) Tenant detail card (selectable tenant): small time series (1h) for tenant_gpu_ms_total, tenant_tokens_total, tenant_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd_est. Also show current tenant_kv_cache_hit_rate.
3) Cache-warmth scatter: x=per_request_cache_warmth_index (buckets: cold/partial/hot), y=latency_p50, point size=avg_token_count. Helps see latency vs cache. 
4) Batch dilution trend: shard_batch_efficiency per shard with per-tenant stacking for last 24h. Flags when efficiency drops below threshold.
5) Trace anchor table (recent 25): links to traces for cold-cache high-cost requests. Columns: time, tenant, model, tokens, latency, trace_link.
6) Cost fairness histogram: distribution of tenant_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd_est normalized by model and sequence_length bin (so we compare apples-to-apples). This targeted binning helps fairness conversations.

Example queries / pseudo-queries (PromQL-like and SQL-ish):
- tenant_gpu_ms_total (PromQL): sum by (tenant_id) (rate(batch_gpu_ms_total[5m]) * (token_count_in_batch / batch_total_tokens))
- tenant_kv_cache_hit_rate: sum by (tenant_id) (rate(requests{kv_hit="true"}[5m])) / sum by (tenant_id) (rate(requests_total[5m]))
- per_request_cache_warmth_index (SQL-ish using feature store): CASE WHEN kv_hit THEN 1 WHEN prompt_hash IN (recent 10, window 2h) THEN 0.5 ELSE 0 END
- cost_per_1k (derive in dashboard): (tenant_gpu_ms_total * ${GPU_USD_PER_MS}) * 1000 / tenant_tokens_total

Tracing and sampling strategy notes:
- Sampling rules: 1% baseline sampling, plus deterministic 100% sampling for requests where per_request_cache_warmth_index == 0 AND token_count_generated > 50 (cold long-tail), plus 100% sampling for latency > p99.
- Trace anchors to stamp in spans: tenant_id, prompt_hash (sha1 truncated), kv_cache_hit boolean, batch_id, batch_size, model_version, gpu_kernel_ms (from runtime). These anchors allow linking traces to metrics quickly.
- Lightweight cold-flow trace: single-span root for receive -> enqueue -> batch-assemble -> invoke-runtime -> gpu-run -> postprocess. Attach kernel_ms to gpu-run span so we can sum/compare with batch-level GPU time.
- Privacy: prompt_hash must be one-way hashed and salted per-tenant to avoid cross-tenant correlation of prompt content. Salt rotation plan needed.

Attribution heuristics (how we divide batch-level GPU time):
- Baseline approach: weight by token_count_generated per request. 
- Correction factor: if kv_cache_hit true, apply 0.35 multiplier to token weight (heuristic: cached tokens cost ~35% of uncached for kernel time). This is tunable; track a metric batch_estimated_unexplained_ms to detect drift.

Alerting proposals (low-noise):
- Cost spike per tenant: when tenant_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd_est deviates > 3x baseline for 30m AND tenant_tokens_total > threshold (so we avoid noise from tiny tenants).
- Cache regression: tenant_kv_cache_hit_rate drops by >20% relative to 24h median for 15m.
- Batching collapse: shard_batch_efficiency below configured floor for 10m.

Operational runbook snippets (for SRE/SE):
- If cost spike alert triggers: open tenant detail -> check cache_hit_rate -> look at batch sizes -> open trace anchor table for recent cold requests -> look for recent model changes, rollouts, or quantization flips (linked artifacts: release tags).
- If cache regression: check prefix hashing logic, redis eviction metrics, or recent model version changes that altered prompt hashing. Search for recent PRs in github:repo/inference-observability#134.

Open questions / follow-ups (next actions):
- Validate kv cache multiplier (0.35) empirically on a sample of batch traces and kernel_ms. Assign to Benji to run mini-benchmark.
- Confirm billing team wants amortized host overhead visible or hidden by default. (Action: Marta to sync).
- Decide on salt rotation cadence for prompt_hash consistency vs privacy (Liam to propose).
- UX: how much filtering should the tenant detail card support (model_version, region)? Quick poll with console team.

Todos (short):
- [ ] Implement PromQL approximations in metrics pipeline (owner: Asha).
- [ ] Add trace sampling rule for cold long-tail (owner: Benji).
- [ ] Mock Grafana dashboard and walk through with SRE (owner: Marta).
- [ ] Run benchmark to sanity-check cache multiplier (owner: Benji).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could show a small per-tenant "cost fairness score" 0..100 derived from normalized cost percentiles after binning by seq_len/model. But be careful: risk of misinterpretation.
- If we add chargeback UI later, we should provide both raw_gpu_ms and adjusted_gpu_ms with clear doc tooltips that explain heuristics.

References and quick links:
- Confluence draft: OBS-COST-PRIME (linked)
- Example trace anchor PR: github:repo/inference-observability#134
- Jira ticket for sampling rules: JIRA:OBS-9876

End of note. This is intentionally terse and experimental. Use as basis for a small sprint to build the dashboard + sampling changes.
